title: Checks for function docstrings that include parameters which are not in the function signature.
summary: If a docstring documents a parameter which is not in the function signature, it can be misleading to users and/or a sign of incomplete documentation or refactors. Ruff takes this rule from pydoclint. It is in preview.
message_templates: Documented parameter `{}` is not in the function's signature

title: Checks for functions with return statements that do not have "Returns" sections in their docstrings.
summary: A missing "Returns" section is a sign of incomplete documentation. Ruff takes this rule from pydoclint. It is in preview.

title: Checks for function docstrings with unnecessary "Returns" sections.
summary: A function without an explicit return statement should not have a "Returns" section in its docstring. Ruff takes this rule from pydoclint. It is in preview.
message_templates: Docstring should not have a returns section because the function doesn't return anything

title: Checks for functions with yield statements that do not have "Yields" sections in their docstrings.
summary: A missing "Yields" section is a sign of incomplete documentation. Ruff takes this rule from pydoclint. It is in preview.

title: Checks for function docstrings with unnecessary "Yields" sections.
summary: A function that doesn't yield anything should not have a "Yields" section in its docstring. Ruff takes this rule from pydoclint. It is in preview.
message_templates: Docstring has a "Yields" section but the function doesn't yield anything

title: Checks for function docstrings that do not document all explicitly raised exceptions.
summary: A function should document all exceptions that are directly raised in some circumstances. Failing to document an exception that could be raised can be misleading to users and/or a sign of incomplete documentation. Ruff takes this rule from pydoclint. It is in preview.

title: Checks for function docstrings that state that exceptions could be raised even though they are not directly raised in the function body.
summary: Some conventions prefer non-explicit exceptions be omitted from the docstring. Ruff takes this rule from pydoclint. It is in preview.
message_templates: Raised exception is not explicitly raised: `{}`
Raised exceptions are not explicitly raised: {}
